subject: Discovery recap + proposed bake-off plan — Stellar Retail evaluation
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily@stellarretail.com>, James Davis <jdavis@stellarretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap + proposed bake-off plan — Stellar Retail evaluation

Hi Emily / James —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed plan so we can move into a hands-on bake-off next week. Please reply with any corrections or missing items.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Production instability and unpredictable tail latencies on current cloud endpoints (esp. during peak traffic).
- High per-token cost at scale for multi-turn chat and embedding pipelines.
- Security requirement to keep PII within a VPC / on-prem option for certain stores.

Current stack you described:
- Model hosting: vLLM + TGI for some internal prototypes; cloud-hosted endpoints for customer-facing chat.
- Frontend: React + Redux; backend services on AWS ECS behind an ALB.
- Data: anonymized chat logs, embeddings for retrieval, and a 20K-item product catalog.

Success criteria (we proposed these during the call):
1) Latency: 95th percentile chat response <= 120 ms for short-turn interactions (<= 256 tokens), and <= 250 ms for longer sequences (<= 1024 tokens) in production-like conditions.
2) Throughput: sustained embedding throughput >= 500 reqs/min for 512-dim vectors (bulk-batch mode).
3) Cost: Total per-1M-token inference cost lower than your current cloud baseline (share current baseline so we can quantify).
4) Quality: parity on your internal reranking metric (MRR) within 5% of the best-performing baseline model you choose for the bake-off.
5) Security & ops: ability to run in your VPC (Private deployment) and provide audit logs/KMS integration.

Proposed bake-off plan (attached template):
- We’ll run two benchmark tracks: Hosted Redwood API vs Dedicated reserved capacity (and a Private VPC trial if you want on-prem-like networking).
- Model variants: float16 FP32 baseline + quantized 8-bit candidate (where applicable).
- Workloads: 1) multi-turn chat (mix of short/long), 2) embedding batch, 3) cold-start cold-KV tests to measure KV cache warm-up.
- Measurements: p50/p95 latency, memory utilization, cost per 1M tokens, throughput, correctness on your MRR test set.

Next steps we need from you to schedule execution:
1) Share an anonymized test dataset (chat logs + MRR eval) or give us a sample subset (S3 link preferred).
2) Confirm expected concurrent users during peak so we can size Dedicated pools.
3) Approve a kickoff window — we’re proposing Aug 5–7 for the first smoke run.
4) Tell us which competitor baseline (vLLM or TGI or your cloud endpoint) you want us to directly compare against in our report.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-template.xlsx (matrix + measurement plan), network-arch-diagram.pdf, rdw-smoke-test-instructions.md

If that looks right I’ll schedule the kickoff and assign an engineer to the run.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184
From: Emily Torres <emily@stellarretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, James Davis <jdavis@stellarretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed bake-off plan — Stellar Retail evaluation

Sean — thanks, this is great and captures the conversation. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency targets: the 95th <= 120ms target is for our customer-facing live chat (short messages, <= 128 tokens). For longer system prompts (policy checks + user history) 95th <= 250ms is acceptable.

2) Cost: we’ll share last quarter’s bill for inference (cloud endpoint spend) — helps set a realistic cost target for per-1M-token comparisons.

3) Security: we must be able to encrypt keys via our AWS KMS and keep logs in our Splunk; any Private deployment must support that.

4) Competitor baseline: we want two baselines — your Hosted Redwood API vs our current cloud endpoints; we also want a side-by-side note on where vLLM/TGI were used in our POC (we saw vLLM perform well at smaller sequence lengths but hit memory churn under multi-concurrent long sessions; TGI required more manual tuning). 

5) Sample data: I uploaded a 5k-row anonymized chat sample and a small MRR eval set (S3): s3://stellar-retail-bakeoff/samples/aug2026-anon.zip

Yes to the proposed Aug 5 smoke run window — we can do Aug 5 at 10am PT for a 60-90m kickoff. I’ll loop in our engineering ops alias (ops@stellarretail.com) for networking/whitelisting.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Torres
Head of AI Product, Stellar Retail
emily@stellarretail.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: bake-off test matrix suggestions

Sean / Avery — quick internal notes before kickoff: 
- I reviewed Emily’s S3 upload. Recommend we run three model-config rows in the template: Hosted FP16, Dedicated FP16 with larger batch window, Dedicated int8 quantized (if supported by the model).
- Include a KV warm-up curve: measure p95 after 0, 10, 100 requests to show cache effects.
- Add a cold-start test (simulate instance spin up) to demonstrate tail risk.
- Ops ask: confirm VPC peering & KMS plan before Aug 5 (Emily cc’d ops). If they want a private deployment trial we need ~48–72h for infra prep.

I’ll prep the initial measurement dashboard and the first draft of the runbook (share once done).

—Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily@stellarretail.com>, James Davis <jdavis@stellarretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>, ops@stellarretail.com
Date: 2026-08-03T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed bake-off plan — Stellar Retail evaluation

Emily / James — great, thanks for the S3 link and for confirming the Aug 5 window. Final notes before kickoff: 

- Kickoff: Aug 5, 10:00 AM PT — 60–90 minutes. I’ll send a calendar invite and include the runbook + pre-checklist.
- Pre-checklist (what we need by EOD Aug 4):
  * VPC egress/ingress rules and a list of CIDRs or peering confirm (ops@stellarretail.com)
  * KMS key ARN for test workspace or instructions for a test KMS role binding
  * Current cloud endpoint billing export (last quarter) for cost baseline
  * Confirmation of the competitor baseline(s) to compare in the final report (vLLM, TGI, cloud endpoint)

- Acceptance criteria restated for the bake-off report: p95 chat latency <= 120ms (short), throughput >= 500 embedding reqs/min, MRR within 5% of best baseline, and Private deployment compatibility if required.

We’ll queue Marissa’s team to run the smoke tests during the kickoff and capture raw logs/metrics. After the smoke run we’ll iterate — full bake-off report expected within 7 business days.

Invite will follow. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
